chapter: Ch 4: Presentation and Disclosures Based Accounting Standards
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction and Objective of AS 24
explain: AS 24 sets rules for reporting information when an enterprise decides to discontinue an operation.
It helps users of financial statements project future cash flows, earnings capacity, and financial position.
It achieves this by clearly separating discontinuing operations from continuing operations.
The standard applies to all discontinuing operations of an enterprise.
Classifying an operation as discontinuing does not by itself question whether the enterprise is a going concern.

flow.title: Objective of AS 24 Reporting
steps: Enterprise decides to discontinue an operation
Segregate discontinuing and continuing activities
Report separate cash flows and earnings
Users make better projections of entity

topics.example: A company manufacturing electronics decides to stop selling televisions; it reports TV operations separately so investors know future earnings depend only on other products.
remember: AS 24 applies to all discontinuing operations without exception.
Discontinuing operation classification alone does not mean the company is no longer a going concern.
mistakes: Assuming that a discontinuing operation automatically means the entire enterprise is failing or violating the going concern assumption.

quiz.q: What is the primary objective of AS 24?
o: To liquidate an enterprise immediately
To segregate discontinuing operations from continuing operations for better user projections
To prevent companies from disposing of loss-making assets
To revalue assets at historical costs
quiz.why: AS 24 aims to segregate discontinuing operations from continuing operations to help users make projections of cash flows and earnings.

quiz.q: Does classifying an operation as a discontinuing operation under AS 24 question the entity's going concern status?
o: Yes, always
Yes, if approved by shareholders
No, it does not in itself question going concern
Only if liabilities exceed assets
quiz.why: AS 24 explicitly states that this classification does not, in itself, bring into question the enterprise's ability to continue as a going concern.

topics.title: Meaning and Criteria of a Discontinuing Operation
explain: A discontinuing operation is a component of an enterprise being disposed of pursuant to a single plan.
Disposal can happen entirely, piecemeal by selling assets and paying liabilities, or via abandonment.
The component must represent a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations.
It can be an AS 17 reportable business or geographical segment, a part of such segment, or a major product or service line.
It must be distinguishable operationally and for financial reporting purposes.
Distinguishability requires directly attributable assets, liabilities, revenues, and at least a majority of operating expenses.

flow.title: Criteria to Qualify as Discontinuing Operation
steps: Single plan of disposal or abandonment
Represents major business line or geography
Distinguishable operationally and financially
Attributable assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses
Qualifies as discontinuing operation

topics.example: An airline group running hotels, software, and flights sells off its airline vertical under one coordinated plan; it meets all three criteria.
remember: Must satisfy all three criteria: single plan, major line/geography, and operationally distinguishable.
At least a majority of operating expenses must be directly attributable to the component.
mistakes: Treating the sale of a single small branch or single restaurant (e.g., 5% revenue) without a coordinated plan as a discontinuing operation.

quiz.q: Which of the following conditions must be met for a component to be distinguished operationally and financially?
o: Only operating assets can be attributed to it
Operating assets, liabilities, revenue, and at least a majority of operating expenses are directly attributable
It must be a separate legal subsidiary entity
It must contribute more than 50% of total company revenue
quiz.why: A component is distinguishable if operating assets, liabilities, revenue, and at least a majority of operating expenses can be directly attributed.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid mode of disposing of a component under a single plan?
o: Disposing of substantially in its entirety
Disposing of piecemeal by selling assets individually
Terminating through abandonment
Normal wear and tear replacement of machinery
quiz.why: Normal asset replacement is an ordinary operational activity, not an abandonment or disposal of a component under a single plan.

topics.title: Activities Not Qualifying on Their Own
explain: Certain activities do not necessarily satisfy the disposal criterion on their own without other circumstances.
Gradual or evolutionary phasing out of a product line or service class is not a discontinuing operation.
Discontinuing several products within an ongoing line of business does not meet the criteria.
Shifting production or marketing activities from one location to another is not a discontinuance.
Closing a facility merely to achieve cost savings or productivity improvements is not covered.
Changing the scope or manner in which an operation is conducted is continuing, not abandonment.

flow.title: Assessing Operational Changes
steps: Operational change or facility closure occurs
Check if merely shifting or phasing out
Check if part of ongoing business revamp
Does not qualify as discontinuing operation
Treated as continuing operation

topics.example: A car maker phases out diesel cars over five years to revamp its factory for electric vehicles; this restructuring is part of continuing operations.
remember: Gradual phasing out by itself is never a discontinuing operation.
Relocating production to cut costs remains a continuing operation.
mistakes: Confusing routine business reorganisations or shifting of factory locations with discontinuing operations.

quiz.q: Which of the following activities on its own satisfies the criterion for a discontinuing operation?
o: Gradual evolutionary phasing out of a product line
Shifting production activities from one plant to another
Closing a facility solely to achieve cost savings
None of the above
quiz.why: None of these activities alone meet criterion (a) unless accompanied by other qualifying circumstances under a single plan.

quiz.q: A company revamps its manufacturing plant to switch from diesel cars to electric cars. This is an example of:
o: Abandonment under AS 24
Changing scope of continuing operations
Disposal of a business line
Spin-off to shareholders
quiz.why: Changing the scope or manner in which an operation is conducted is not abandonment because the operation continues in a changed form.

topics.title: Initial Disclosure Event
explain: The initial disclosure event triggers the mandatory reporting requirements under AS 24.
It is the earlier of two events: entering a binding sale agreement, or board approval plus formal announcement.
The binding sale agreement must cover substantially all assets attributable to the operation.
A formal plan approved by the board must include assets, disposal method, completion period, locations, affected employees, and estimated proceeds.
An announcement is effective only if made to affected parties (e.g., lenders, unions, stock exchanges) making the entity demonstrably committed.

flow.title: Determining the Initial Disclosure Event
steps: Check date of binding sale agreement
Check date of board approval plus announcement
Compare the two occurrence dates
Earlier date is Initial Disclosure Event
Triggers AS 24 disclosures in reporting period

topics.example: Board approves and announces a closure plan on 15th March 20X1, and signs the sale contract on 1st July 20X1. The initial disclosure event date is 15th March 20X1.
remember: Earlier of: (1) Binding sale agreement, or (2) Board approval AND announcement.
Both approval AND public announcement to affected parties are required to complete the second option.
mistakes: Selecting only the board resolution date when the public announcement was made on a later date.
Choosing the balance sheet reporting date instead of the actual event date.

quiz.q: Board approves a discontinuing plan on 1st March, announces it to unions on 15th March, and signs a binding sale agreement on 1st July. When is the initial disclosure event?
o: 1st March
15th March
1st July
31st March
quiz.why: Board approval plus formal announcement was completed on 15th March, which is earlier than the binding agreement on 1st July.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT typically included in a detailed formal plan for discontinuance?
o: Expected method of disposal
Audit fees of the statutory auditor
Major assets to be disposed of
Locations and employees affected
quiz.why: Statutory audit fees are general enterprise expenses and not part of the formal discontinuance plan details.

topics.title: Recognition, Measurement, and Disclosures
explain: AS 24 does not provide principles for recognition and measurement; relevant other accounting standards must be followed.
Disclosures begin in the financial statements for the period in which the initial disclosure event occurs.
Initial disclosures in notes include description, segment info, date/nature of event, expected completion timing, assets and liabilities amounts, and cash flows.
Pre-tax profit/loss of the discontinuing operation and related tax expense must be shown directly on the face of the Profit and Loss statement.
Pre-tax gain/loss recognized on disposal of assets or settlement of liabilities must also appear on the face of the Profit and Loss statement.
Other disclosures upon disposal include pre-tax gain/loss, tax expense, net selling prices, expected timing of cash flows, and carrying amounts.

flow.title: Presentation Location of AS 24 Disclosures
steps: Identify required disclosures
Place pre-tax profit/loss on face of P&L
Place pre-tax disposal gain/loss on face of P&L
Place related income tax on face of P&L
Present all other details in Notes

topics.example: A company reports €2,00,000 profit from an abandoned division and €30,000 tax directly on the face of its Profit and Loss account, detailing the cash flows in the notes.
remember: Face of P&L: Pre-tax operating profit/loss, related tax, and pre-tax gain/loss on disposal of net assets.
Notes to accounts: Assets, liabilities, cash flows, segment, and descriptions.
mistakes: Putting operating cash flows of the discontinuing operation on the face of the Profit and Loss statement instead of the notes.
Thinking AS 24 specifies its own asset impairment measurement rules instead of referring to other standards.

quiz.q: Which item relating to a discontinuing operation must be presented on the face of the statement of profit and loss?
o: Carrying amounts of assets to be disposed of
Net operating, investing, and financing cash flows
Pre-tax profit or loss of the discontinuing operation and related tax expense
Description of the discontinuing operation
quiz.why: Pre-tax profit/loss and related tax expense must appear on the face of the statement of profit and loss.

quiz.q: Where does AS 24 get its recognition and measurement rules for discontinuing operations?
o: From AS 24 itself
It refers to relevant other Accounting Standards
From international tax treaties
From the Companies Act Schedule III only
quiz.why: AS 24 does not provide separate recognition and measurement guidelines; relevant other Accounting Standards must be followed.

topics.title: Updating Disclosures, Prior Period Restatement, and Interim Reporting
explain: Disclosures must be updated in subsequent periods for significant changes in amount or timing of cash flows.
Reporting continues until the period when the discontinuance plan is substantially completed or abandoned.
If a plan is abandoned or withdrawn, that fact, the reasons, and the financial effects must be disclosed.
Separate disclosures must be given for each separate discontinuing operation.
Comparative prior period figures must be restated to segregate continuing and discontinuing operations.
Interim reports under AS 25 must disclose significant activities/events and changes in cash flow timing since the last annual report.

flow.title: Ongoing Compliance Lifecycle
steps: Initial disclosure period passes
Update cash flow changes in next periods
Restate prior period comparative figures
Report interim updates under AS 25
Continue until plan is substantially completed

topics.example: A firm selling a division in Year 2 must restate Year 1 comparative income statement figures to show that division separately as discontinuing.
remember: Prior period comparative statements must be restated to segregate discontinuing and continuing operations.
Full receipt of cash is not required for completion; substantial completion of the plan ends the cycle.
mistakes: Assuming comparative prior period figures should not be altered or restated.
Waiting until all customer payments are collected before considering the discontinuance completed.

quiz.q: When is a discontinuance considered completed under AS 24?
o: Only when all sale proceeds are 100% collected in bank
When the plan is substantially completed or abandoned
Exactly 12 months after board approval
When all employees retire
quiz.why: Discontinuance is completed when the plan is substantially completed or abandoned, even if full payments have not yet been received.

quiz.q: What must an enterprise do regarding comparative figures of prior periods after an initial disclosure event?
o: Leave prior period figures completely unchanged
Delete prior period columns entirely
Restate prior periods to segregate continuing and discontinuing operations
Add all prior period numbers into current year revenue
quiz.why: Comparative information for prior periods must be restated to segregate assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, and cash flows.
